title: Acceptance criteria for Private deployment: split-horizon DNS, constrained egress, and offline upgrade paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures requirements and measurable acceptance criteria for Private/VPC customer deployments where (a) DNS is split-horizon or nonstandard, (b) egress is constrained or proxied, and (c) upgrades must support air-gapped or intermittent-network environments. The goal is to define what engineering must deliver and how Product will validate it prior to GA for private installs. Scope covers networking expectations, upgrade bundle formats, certificate handling, runtime connectivity checks, and observable validation steps.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Installer supports configurable split-horizon DNS: customer may provide an ordered list of resolver endpoints and domain overrides; installer validates resolution of all Redwood control-plane FQDNs against provided resolvers before completing install.

AC-2: Egress proxy support: runtime components can be configured with HTTP(S) proxy and mTLS egress proxy; integration test demonstrates model pull, license check, and telemetry buffering through a customer-controlled proxy with token-based auth.

AC-3: Offline upgrade bundle: engineering provides an image bundle and a signed manifest that can be transported into an air-gapped environment; upgrade can be executed end-to-end from bundle with no external connectivity and completes rollback on failure within two minutes where applicable.

AC-4: Partial-network scenarios: platform components expose a diagnostic endpoint that returns a deterministic checklist (DNS, proxy, NTP, KMS reachability) and installer refuses to proceed if any critical item is failing; diagnostic output must include error codes mapping to remediation actions.

AC-5: Certificate lifecycle in air-gapped environments: mechanism to provision and rotate TLS certs using customer-provided CA bundles; documentation and CLI accept PEM files for bootstrapping and rotation without internet access.

AC-6: Upgrade compatibility gates: release image signing must be validated locally against customer CA/HSM, and delta upgrades (patch image + manifest) must support validation and rollback when signature or checksum mismatch is detected.

AC-7: Observability for networking faults: Console traces and logs must surface (a) DNS failures, (b) proxy auth failures, (c) blocked egress endpoints, and (d) upgrade validation failures with token-level and route-level attribution where possible.

AC-8: Test harness: provide an automated test harness (runnable in customer VPC or CI) that emulates split-horizon DNS and intermittent egress and outputs a PASS/FAIL with artifacts (pcap, dig outputs, installer logs) for each test case.

AC-9: Docs and runbook: ship a runbook for SRE/customer operator with step-by-step troubleshooting for the 10 most common failure modes; runbook must include sample internal DNS policies, proxy configuration snippets, and rollback commands.
AC-10: Backward compatibility: Private installations created under previous private-2024.x must be upgradeable with the provided offline bundle with no manual state migration steps.

AC-Extra: Performance constraint: diagnostic and validation checks must complete within 90 seconds on typical customer networks; any step that exceeds this must surface as a WARN rather than silently timing out.
implementation_notes: Implementation should add a network-validate subcommand to the private installer that runs resolvers, proxy handshake checks, TLS chain validation, and a simulated model artifact pull (without pulling large blobs).
Installer must accept --resolvers (comma list), --host-overrides file, --egress-proxy settings, and --offline-bundle path. Return codes documented in runbook.
Upgrade bundles to be signed using existing image-signing flow; manifest format v2 includes list of images, checksums, and pre/post hooks. Engineering to finalize spec and publish example bundles.
For mTLS proxy support, provide a lib/proxy-auth shim in the runtime that can load client certs from disk or KMS; integration test to simulate proxy injection in CI.

Telemetry and logs from private installs must be redacted by default (PII) and opt-in for sending to Redwood control plane; for air-gapped installs, provide local log-export tools documented in runbook.
test_plan: TP-1: Acceptance lab (internal): Deploy private cluster in isolated VPC with a split-horizon DNS setup. Run network-validate; assert all checks pass and installer proceeds to complete installation.
TP-2: Proxy gating test: Configure a transparent HTTP proxy that requires mTLS client certs. Validate model artifact download and telemetry buffering succeed through proxy.
TP-3: Air-gap upgrade test: Simulate air-gapped upgrade by transferring offline bundle to the host. Run upgrade path and intentionally corrupt manifest to verify rollback behavior.
TP-4: Intermittent egress: Introduce packet loss to the control-plane endpoints and verify installer retry/backoff behavior and deterministic diagnostic outputs.
TP-5: Regression: run existing private-2024.x upgrade tests to confirm no regressions in state migration and RBAC behaviors.
decisions: D1: Use signed offline bundles with manifest v2 instead of shipping a bespoke binary-only installer to simplify validation and reuse image-signing infra.
D2: Prioritize DNS and proxy validation checks in installer over aggressive auto-fallbacks; we will not implicitly rewrite customer DNS or install network agents without explicit opt-in.
D3: Expose failure codes and remediation actions rather than opaque error strings to reduce operator troubleshooting time.
open_questions: Q1: Should the diagnostic checker attempt to auto-probe KMS endpoints or only validate network connectivity to the host-specified KMS gateway?
Q2: For delta upgrades in air-gapped setups, what's the acceptable maximum bundle size and will we offer a streaming/patch-based delta format to reduce transfer costs?
Q3: How will enterprise customers want to handle telemetry and crash reports from private installs; require opt-in flags and clear data retention guidance?
Q4: Is HSM-backed signature verification required at GA or can we ship with local CA file verification and add HSM integration in a subsequent release?
